title: protium tenuifolium subsp. sessiliflorum
intro: Protium tenuifolium subsp. sessiliflorum, commonly known as the Brazilian cherry or 'pau-ferro', is a species of plant in the family Burseraceae. It has been traditionally used in folk medicine due to its potential health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which can aid in reducing pain, fighting infections, and protecting against cell damage. The bioactive constituents present in this plant include flavonoids, terpenoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its therapeutic actions, such as analgesic, anti-inflammatory, and antiproliferative effects. Further research is needed to fully understand the efficacy and safety of Protium tenuifolium subsp. sessiliflorum for medicinal use.
